method_history.1_in_game_3d_render_injection: Wrote a synthetic contact record (position, action_id=target kind, +0x28/+0x2A quad size) into a free pool slot, using an actively-managed slot's full byte layout as a template so implicit invariants weren't guessed. PROVEN to trigger real renders: the objective per-frame draw-flag bit (+0x32 bit0, per analysis/phase4_contact_object_render.json's measured pipeline) confirmed drawn=True for 24/26 tested kinds, and drawn=False for kind 0 -- exactly matching that artifact's own documented fact that action_id 0 is the renderer's explicit 'do not draw' sentinel. Real methodology bugs found and fixed along the way: active_type (+0x22) is a countdown, not a flag (a hand-built record with active_type=500 still hit 0 in ~2 frames when other implicit fields didn't match what real game-managed records look like; copying a REAL active record's full byte layout fixed it). gpu.pickObject's returned 'ramAddress' is a GPU draw-command buffer address, not the CPU contact-record address -- do not compare them.
method_history.2_REJECTED_screenshot_sampling: Captured in-game frames and sampled sprite pixel colour. DECISIVELY INVALIDATED before banking anything: colours cycled with an EXACT PERIOD OF 8 across the test batch, completely unrelated to which kind was set (kind 3's sampled colour == kind 14's == kind 28's, exactly) -- almost certainly dithering/anti-aliasing noise from the in-game 3D pipeline at this tiny sprite scale, not real per-kind signal. This method could not distinguish kinds and its results are NOT used for any classification below.
method_history.3_direct_vram_texture_decode: gpu.decodeTexture at the descriptor's own exact (TPAGE, CLUT, u0, v0, width, height) -- bypasses the 3D pipeline, dithering, scale and blur entirely. VALIDATED first against kind 20 (grain, already Canon-bound): produced a clean, unmistakable single grain-kernel icon. This is the method used for every classification below.
